header: Ayesha Jamil and two others vs. Muhammad Saeed and
For petitioner Mr. Muhammad Ali, Advocate
For respondents Mr. Sajjad Ahmad Mehsud, Advocate
body: MUHAMMAD NAEEM ANWAR, J: - Through the instant constitutional petition, Ayesha Jamil and her two minor children have called into question the judgment & order dated 22/04/2026 passed by the learned Additional District Judge- VIII/Family Appellate Court-I, Peshawar, whereby their appeal against the order dated 28/02/2026 passed by the learned Judge, Family Court-II, Peshawar, was dismissed. Through the latter order, the application filed by respondent No.1, Muhammad Saad, seeking interim custody of petitioners No.2 and 3 was allowed, with a direction to petitioner No.1 to hand over the minors to respondent No.1 during the ongoing or next scheduled school vacation, strictly in accordance with the terms of the joint statement previously recorded between the parties before the learned Family Court.
2. Arguments heard and the available record perused.

3. Before addressing the rival contentions, it is necessary to recapitulate the relevant background and examine the nature of the arrangement mutually agreed upon by the parties, as well as the circumstances that have emerged since their separation. The record reflects that petitioner No.1, Ayesha Jamil, and respondent No.1, Muhammad Saad, contracted marriage on 29/10/2016, and their wedlock was blessed with two children, namely, Manal Saad and Hassan Sultan, presently stated to be approximately eight and seven years of age, respectively. Unfortunately, matrimonial discord developed between the parties, giving rise to litigation concerning dissolution of marriage, dower, maintenance of petitioner No.1 and the minors, and the return of dowry articles. Petitioner No.1 instituted proceedings in her own capacity, while respondent No.1 also instituted separate proceedings. Both sets of proceedings were consolidated for adjudication. During the pendency of the consolidated proceedings, the parties arrived at a settlement on 14/07/2025, whereupon their respective claims were disposed of in accordance with their joint statement. Since the present controversy primarily concerns the nature and implementation of the arrangement agreed upon regarding the minors, the relevant portion of their joint statement, originally recorded in Urdu, is reproduced below:

ٖﻣﺸﺘﺮکہ ﺑﻴﺎﻥ ﻓﺮﻳﻘﻴﻦ ﻣﺤﻤﺪ ﺳﻌﺪ ﻭﻟﺪ ﻣﺤﻤﺪ ﺍٓﻳﺎﺯ )ﻣﺪﻋی( ﻣﻘﺪﻣہ ﻧﻤﺒﺮ ◌ٖ180/FCﻣﺪﻋی ﻣﺴﻤﺎﺓ ﻋﺎﺋﺸہ ﺟﻤﻴﻞ ﺩﺧﺘﺮﺣﺎﻣﺪ ﺟﻤﻴﻞ)ﻣﺪﻋﻴہ( ﻣﻘﺪﻣہ64/FCﻣﺪﻋﺎﻋﻠﻴہ ﺣﻠﻔﺎ ٰ ﺑﻴﺎﻥ کﺮﺗےہﻴں کہ ﻣﺎﺑﻴﻦ ﻓﺮﻳﻘﻴﻦ ﺗﻨﺴﻴﺦ ﻧکﺎﺡ ﺑﺬﺭﻳﻌہ ﺧﻠﻊ ہﻮ چکﺎ ہے ﺍﻭﺭ ﻣﺪﻋﻴہ ﻋﺎﺋﺸہﺟﻤﻴﻞ ﺣﻖ ﻣہﺮ ﺳے ﺑﺤﻖ ﻣﺪﻋﺎﻋﻠﻴہ ﻣﺤﻤﺪ ﺳﻌﺪ ﺩﺳﺘﺒﺮﺩﺍﺭ ہﻮﺗی ہے۔ ﺗﺎ ہﻢ ﻣﺪﻋﺎﻋﻠﻴہ ﻣﺤﻤﺪ ﺳﻌﺪﻣﺪﻋﻴہ کﺎ ﺳﺎﻣﺎﻥ ﺟہﻴﺰ ﺍﻧﺪﺭ ﻣﻴﻌﺎﺩ ﺍﻳک ہﻔﺘہ ﻭﺍپﺲ کﺮﻧے کﺎ پﺎﺑﻨﺪ ہﻮ گﺎ۔ﻧﻴﺰ ﻧﺎﺑﺎﻟﻐﺎﻥﻋﺎﺋﺸہﺟﻤﻴﻞ کے پﺎﺱ ہﻮںگے۔ ﺟﺴکﺎ ﺧﺮچہ ﺧﻮﺭﺍکہ ﻣﺪﻋﺎﻋﻠﻴہ ﻣﺤﻤﺪ ﺳﻌﺪ ﺑﻤﻄﺎﺑﻖ ﻗﺎﻧﻮﻥ ﺍﺩﺍ کﺮﺗﺎ ﺭہے گﺎ)ﺑﺸﺮﺡ ﻣﺒﻠﻎ ﺩﺱ ہﺰﺍﺭ ﻓی ﻧﺎﺑﺎﻟﻎ (ﺗﺎہﻢ ﻣﺪﻋﺎﻋﻠﻴہﻧﺎﺑﺎﻟﻐﺎﻥ ﺳے ﺳپﺮﻳﻢ کﻮﺭٹ کی ﺟﺎﻧﺐ ﺳے ﻣﻘﺮﺭ کﺮﺩﻩscheduleﺩﺭ ﻣﻘﺪﻣہ SCMR 19912018کﺮﻧے کﺎ ﺣﻖﺭکﻬﺘﺎ ہے۔ﺟﺲ پﺮ ﻣﺪﻋﻴہ ﻋﺎءﺷہ ﺟﻤﻴﻞ کﻮ کﻮﻳیﺍﻋﺘﺮﺍﺽ ﻧہﻴں ہے۔ ﺍﺳﺘﺪﻋﺎ ہے کہ ﻓﺮﻳﻘﻴﻦ کے ﻣﻘﺪﻣﺎﺕﻣﻨﺪﺭﺟہﺑﺎﻻ ﺑﻴﺎﻥ ﺣﻠﻔی کیٔ ﺭﻭ ﺳے ﻓﻴﺼﻠہ ﻓﺮﻣﺎے۔ ﻧﻘﻮﻻﺕCNIC،EX: PAﻭEX: PBہﻴں۔ The aforesaid statement culminated in an order recognizing the right of respondent No.1 to meet the minors in accordance with the visitation schedule laid down by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Mst. Madiha Younas v. Imran Ahmad (2018 SCMR 1991). The settlement, therefore, expressly recognized the mother's custody of the minors, the father's obligation to maintain them, and his entitlement to visitation in accordance with the prescribed schedule.

4. Following the settlement dated 14/07/2025, respondent No.1 approached the learned District Judge, Peshawar, by filing an application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, on 29/07/2025. The application was dismissed by the learned Additional District Judge, Peshawar/Child Protection Court, on 30/07/2025. Subsequently, on 08/01/2026, respondent No.1 approached the learned Family Court through an application seeking interim custody of the minors, invoking the arrangement recorded in the joint statement. The application was contested by the present petitioners; nevertheless, the learned Family Court allowed it and directed petitioner No.1 to hand over interim custody of the minors to respondent No.1, subject to furnishing a surety bond in the sum of Rs. 1,000,000/- to the satisfaction of the Court. The petitioners challenged that order before the learned appellate Court, but their appeal was dismissed through the impugned judgment and order dated 22/04/2026, giving rise to the instant petition.

5. During the pendency of this petition, respondent No.1 was put on notice. Having regard to the immediate need to restore and facilitate contact between the father and his children, this Court, through order dated 16/06/2026, made an interim arrangement for supervised visitation. The operative portion of the said order reads as follows: “Accordingly, it is ordered, as an interim arrangement, that on every Saturday, commencing from 09:00 am. till 03:00 p.m., respondent No.1 shall appear before the learned Judge, Family Court/Executing Court, where he shall be allowed to meet and interact with the minors/petitioners No.2 and 3 within the Court premises and under the supervision of the Court, till the rising of the Court. This arrangement shall continue for a period of four consecutive Saturdays, so as to facilitate restoration of interaction and emotional bonding between respondent No.1 and the minors in a congenial and nonconfrontational atmosphere.

It is further observed that upon completion of the aforesaid four meetings, the instant petition shall be taken up for hearing for appropriate determination of a structured visitation schedule between the parties, including any arrangement concerning overnight stay or extended visitation, in the context of the order impugned in the present petition. The matter is accordingly adjourned to 20.07.2026. The parties are directed to appear before the learned Judge, Family Court-II, on 29.06.2026 at exactly 09:00 a.m., for implementation of the interim arrangement.

It is further directed that during the course of visitation or interaction with the minors, respondent No.1 shall refrain from causing any harassment, intimidation, inconvenience, or discomfort to petitioner No.1 in any manner whatsoever. In case petitioner No.1 experiences or reasonably apprehends any such conduct, she shall be at liberty to approach this Court by moving an appropriate application at any time during the intervening period for appropriate remedial directions.
Respondent No.1 is also directed to continue payment of the monthly maintenance of the minors regularly and punctually, strictly in accordance with law and the orders already in the field.”

The aforesaid arrangement was intended to facilitate the gradual restoration of interaction and emotional bonding between the father and the minors in a safe, supervised and non-confrontational environment, without prejudicing the final determination of the controversy regarding the appropriate scope and duration of visitation.

6. One of the principal grievances raised by the petitioners was that respondent No.1 had failed to discharge his obligation to pay maintenance and that arrears remained outstanding against him. Having considered the said objection, this Court directed respondent No.1 to clear the entire outstanding amount before the learned Executing Court. Today, respondent No.1 has produced a copy of the order dated 13/10/2026 passed by the learned Executing Court, which reflects satisfaction of the outstanding maintenance liability. Consequently, the grievance of the petitioners concerning the arrears of maintenance stands redressed to that extent. Nevertheless, respondent No.1 remains under a continuing obligation to pay the maintenance of the minors regularly and punctually in accordance with the subsisting orders of the competent Court.

7. The material circumstances relevant to the determination of an appropriate visitation arrangement are that the parties have been living separately since 14/07/2025, while their relationship had already become strained during 2024. Throughout this period, the minors have remained in the custody of their mother, petitioner No.1. Respondent No.1 contracted a second marriage approximately thirteen to fourteen months ago, and a child has also been born from that marriage. He is engaged in business as a shopkeeper and, according to the information placed before this Court, ordinarily remains occupied with his work for substantial periods. It has further been brought to the Court's notice that one of the minors is autistic and requires particular attention, specialized care and a routine responsive to the child's individual needs. The Court is conscious that the circumstances of each minor must be considered individually, notwithstanding their common parentage. In particular, the needs of a child with autism cannot be treated as incidental or overlooked while devising a visitation schedule. Such a child may require consistency, predictability, a familiar environment and appropriate preparation for changes in routine. The nature and degree of the child's individual needs, however, must be assessed on the basis of reliable information rather than assumptions arising merely from the diagnosis. Any arrangement for visitation must, therefore, be sufficiently structured and flexible to accommodate the needs of both minors, without exposing either child to avoidable distress or disruption.

8. The paramount consideration governing every determination concerning the custody and visitation of minors is their welfare. Such welfare is neither synonymous with the preference of either parent nor may it be compromised by the grievances arising from the failed matrimonial relationship. It embraces their physical and emotional well-being, education, health, psychological security, social development and the opportunity to maintain meaningful relationships with both parents, insofar as such relationships are consistent with their best interests. The dissolution of the parents' marriage terminates their matrimonial relationship, but it does not extinguish their respective responsibilities towards their children. Equally, the fact that the minors have remained in the mother's custody since separation does not, by itself, justify the permanent exclusion of the father from their lives. Subject to the paramount consideration of the minors' welfare, a child ordinarily benefits from the opportunity to develop and maintain a healthy relationship with both parents. The father’s entitlement to reasonable access and visitation is, therefore, a legally recognized aspect of the parent-child relationship, which cannot be defeated merely because the parents are no longer on cordial terms. That entitlement, however, is neither absolute nor independent of the welfare principle; its manner, duration and conditions must remain responsive to the needs and circumstances of the minors. In addition, the parties' joint statement expressly acknowledged the entitlement of respondent No.1 to meet the minors in accordance with the schedule referred to therein. The arrangement was incorporated into the order disposing of their proceedings and was, therefore, not merely an informal understanding. If respondent No.1 considered that the agreed visitation arrangement was not being implemented, the appropriate course was to seek its enforcement, clarification or suitable modification before the competent Court. The mere existence of the earlier settlement did not, without further consideration of the minors' present circumstances, automatically warrant the grant of interim custody or overnight access. The distinction between a right of visitation and a transfer of custody is material and must be maintained.

9. At the same time, the absence of a sufficiently detailed or practically workable schedule appears to have contributed to the continuation of the dispute. The parties' failure to cooperate in implementing their arrangement cannot be permitted to deprive the minors of a meaningful relationship with their father. Nor should the minors be placed in the midst of their parents' disagreement or made to bear the emotional consequences of their mutual distrust. The judicial response must, therefore, be directed towards an effective, enforceable and child-centered arrangement rather than an adversarial determination of which parent is to blame for the breakdown in communication. This Court has already afforded respondent No.1 an opportunity to meet the minors under judicial supervision pursuant to the order dated 16/06/2026. The interim arrangement was intended to facilitate gradual reintroduction and continuity of contact. Having regard to the history of separation, the strained relationship between the parents, the continued residence of the minors with their mother, and the particular needs of one of the children, the Court is not presently persuaded that overnight stay or an immediate extension of visitation beyond a supervised setting would necessarily advance their welfare. Such an arrangement should not be introduced merely on the basis of the father's entitlement to access, without due regard to the minors' readiness, their emotional comfort and the practical capacity of the proposed arrangement to meet their individual needs. Conversely, an arrangement confined indefinitely to a brief meeting within the Court premises would not, without a proper assessment of the circumstances, necessarily serve the long-term objective of preserving and strengthening the parentchild relationship. Supervision should operate as a protective and transitional measure, not as an instrument to frustrate or unduly restrict visitation. The schedule must accordingly provide regular and meaningful contact, while leaving room for a gradual review and expansion if the experience of the minors and the assessment of the competent Court demonstrate that such progression is in their best interests.

10. In these circumstances, the appropriate course is to prescribe a structured arrangement for supervised visitation on alternate Saturdays, under the control and supervision of the learned Judge, Family Court-II, Peshawar, who is also dealing with the execution proceedings. This will provide certainty to the parties, minimize direct confrontation between them and ensure that any difficulty arising during implementation can be addressed promptly by the Court having immediate oversight of the arrangement. The following directions are, therefore, issued:

i. Respondent No.1 shall be entitled to meet and interact with petitioners No.2 and 3 on every alternate Saturday, from 09:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., at the premises of the learned Family Court-II, Peshawar, or in a suitable room attached thereto, as may be designated by the learned Judge, Family Court/Executing Court. Petitioner No.1 shall produce the minors before the said Court at the appointed time and shall ensure their availability for the scheduled visitation. The meeting shall take place in a congenial, safe and child-friendly environment under the supervision and control of the learned Judge or an officer designated by the Court for that purpose.

ii. During the scheduled visitation, respondent No.1 shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to interact with the minors without unnecessary interruption or interference by petitioner No.1. Equally, respondent No.1 shall conduct himself in a manner conducive to the minors' comfort and emotional security and shall refrain from any act or conversation likely to expose them to the parents' matrimonial disputes, mutual allegations or other adult conflicts. Neither parent shall use the visitation arrangement as a means of harassing, intimidating, humiliating or inconveniencing the other.

iii. Both parents shall cooperate in the implementation of the visitation schedule and shall avoid unnecessary direct confrontation. Petitioner No.1 shall not obstruct visitation on grounds unrelated to the minors' welfare, while respondent No.1 shall respect the boundaries and conditions prescribed by the Court. Any genuine concern relating to the safety, health, emotional well-being or special needs of either minor shall be brought before the learned Family Court/Executing Court through an appropriate application and shall be considered on its merits. Neither party shall unilaterally alter, suspend or frustrate the arrangement except where an immediate and genuine concern for a minor's safety or health necessitates protective action, in which event the matter shall promptly be brought to the Court's attention.

iv. In view of the special care and attention required by the minor who is autistic, the learned Family Court/Executing Court shall ensure that the visitation arrangement accommodates that child's individual needs, including any reasonable requirements concerning routine, communication, sensory comfort, medical care or professional advice, where relevant and supported by the available information. The parties shall not compel the child to participate in a manner that causes avoidable distress. If necessary, the learned Court may seek an appropriate professional assessment or obtain such information as may assist it in determining how visitation can be conducted in the best interests of the child. The needs of the other minor shall likewise be duly considered, and neither child shall be made to feel responsible for the parents' disagreement.

v. Respondent No.1 shall continue to pay the maintenance allowance of both minors regularly and punctually, in accordance with the orders already passed by the competent Court. The satisfaction of the arrears, as reflected in the order dated 13/10/2026, does not absolve him of his continuing monthly obligation. Maintenance and visitation are distinct legal obligations, and neither shall be used as a bargaining instrument to defeat the lawful rights or welfare of the minors. Any alleged default in maintenance shall be addressed through the appropriate execution proceedings in accordance with law.

vi. Respondent No.1 shall be at liberty to approach the learned Family Court/Executing Court through an appropriate application for progressive enlargement of visitation, including extended hours or overnight stay, if he considers that the circumstances warrant such relief. The learned Court shall decide any such application independently, after affording both parties an opportunity of hearing and considering the minors' ages, wishes and emotional readiness to the extent appropriate, their educational routine, the particular needs of the child with autism, the suitability of the proposed arrangements at the father's residence, the quality and consistency of the interaction achieved during supervised meetings, and any other factor relevant to their welfare. The decision shall be based on the circumstances then prevailing and shall not be influenced by any observation in the impugned orders or in the present judgment that may be construed as a conclusive determination regarding future overnight or extended visitation.

vii. The learned Family Court/Executing Court shall retain supervisory control over the arrangement and may, upon a reasoned assessment of the circumstances and the experience of the scheduled meetings, modify the venue, timings or other conditions of visitation where necessary in the best interests of the minors. Any progressive enlargement of visitation shall be guided by the minors' welfare and readiness rather than by a rigid timetable or the unilateral preference of either parent.

11. It is emphasized that the parents must distinguish their personal grievances from their continuing obligations towards their children. Their matrimonial relationship may have come to an end, but their shared responsibility for the upbringing, education, health and future of the minors remains. Each parent must respect the other's legitimate parental role, refrain from speaking adversely about the other in the presence of the children, and avoid conduct that places the minors in a conflict of loyalty. The object of visitation is not to confer an advantage upon one parent over the other; it is to preserve and nurture the minors' relationship with their father in a manner compatible with their security, dignity and developmental needs. The arrangement directed herein is intended to strike a fair balance between the father's right to maintain contact with his children and the paramount requirement of safeguarding their welfare. It shall not be construed as a final determination of any future claim concerning custody or extended visitation, which must remain open to consideration on the basis of the circumstances then existing and the welfare of the minors.

12. For the foregoing reasons, the instant petition is disposed of in the above terms. The impugned order is modified accordingly. The learned Family Court/Executing Court shall ensure implementation of the schedule and shall deal with any application arising therefrom expeditiously and in accordance with law. There shall be no order as to costs. Announced.
J U D G E Ashfaq Ahmad (SB) Hon’ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Naeem Anwar
